title: salix × sendaica subsp. ultima
intro: Salix × sendaica subsp. ultima, commonly known as Japanese white willow, is a subspecies of willow tree native to East Asia. This plant is valued for its potential health benefits, including reducing inflammation and relieving pain, which are attributed to its therapeutic actions such as analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects. Bioactive constituents present in Japanese white willow include salicin, a compound similar to aspirin, which is responsible for its analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Japanese white willow are also thought to be mediated by its flavonoids and phenolic acids, which contribute to its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects.
